references.text: The same context regarding an ox known to be a gorer, and the owner's liability when he has been warned previously (מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם - 'from yesterday and the day before')
Nearby verses dealing with compensation for damage caused by livestock, including the principle of paying full restitution
Laws regarding compensation for damage to another's property, with the principle of full restitution (שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם)
The principle of restitution and retribution in Israelite law
The principle of paying back multiple times when caught stealing, parallel to the principle of restitution
Contrastive parallel: 21:28 establishes acquittal for unknown danger, emphasizing that guilt in 21:36 is conditional on knowledge.
Theological foundational principle: Lev 24:18 establishes the 'life for life' principle which underpins the duty of restitution in Ex 21:36.
Complementary rule: 22:11 (here 7) shows when one does *not* pay (for a predator), sharply defining when one *must* pay in 21:36.
